words.english_meaning: Light, fine rain falling in very small drops.
words.gujarati_meaning: હળવો, ઝીણો વરસાદ — જ્યારે ખૂબ નાના ટીપાં ધીમે ધીમે પડે છે.
words.usage_note: Used for very light rain; less intense than a shower.
examples: There was a light drizzle this morning.
We walked through the drizzle without umbrellas.
The drizzle made the roads slippery.
A gentle drizzle fell on the garden.

words.english_meaning: A heavy and sudden fall of rain.
words.gujarati_meaning: અચાનક અને ભારે વરસાદ — જ્યારે ખૂબ ઝડપથી ઘણો વરસાદ પડે.
words.usage_note: Implies a sudden, intense burst of rain, often unexpected.
words.memory_tip: 'Down' = નીચે + 'pour' = રેડવું → ઉપરથી ઘણો વરસાદ રેડાય.
examples: We were caught in a sudden downpour.
The downpour flooded the streets within minutes.
A downpour interrupted the outdoor wedding.
After the downpour, the sky cleared up.

words.english_meaning: Covered with clouds; dull and grey sky.
words.gujarati_meaning: આકાશ વાદળોથી ઢંકાયેલું — ધૂંધળું અને રાખોડી રંગનું આકાશ.
words.usage_note: Describes a sky completely covered by cloud with no sun visible.
examples: The sky was overcast all day.
An overcast morning turned into heavy rain.
We postponed the picnic because it was overcast.
The overcast weather made everyone feel gloomy.

words.english_meaning: Having a high level of moisture in the air; damp and warm.
words.gujarati_meaning: હવામાં ભેજ વધારે હોય — ગરમ અને ભેજવાળી હવા.
words.usage_note: Often used with 'hot' to describe uncomfortable tropical weather.
words.memory_tip: 'Humid' → humidity → ભેજ. ભેજ = ભારે ગરમી + ભેજ.
examples: Mumbai is extremely humid in summer.
The humid air made it hard to breathe.
We prefer dry heat over humid conditions.
The humid weather caused the wood to swell.

words.english_meaning: Very dry, with little or no rainfall; barren.
words.gujarati_meaning: ખૂબ શુષ્ક — જ્યાં વરસાદ ભાગ્યે જ પડે અને વનસ્પતિ ઓછી હોય.
words.usage_note: Used to describe very dry climates or regions like deserts.
examples: The Sahara is one of the most arid regions on Earth.
Few plants can survive in such arid conditions.
The arid soil cracked under the scorching sun.
Water conservation is essential in arid climates.

words.english_meaning: A very strong wind, typically reaching 50–100 km/h.
words.gujarati_meaning: ખૂબ જોરદાર પવન — સામાન્ય રીતે ૫૦ થી ૧૦૦ કિ.મી./કલાકની ઝડપે ફૂંકાય.
words.usage_note: A gale is stronger than a breeze but weaker than a hurricane.
examples: The gale knocked down several trees.
Sailors were warned about gale-force winds.
The gale made walking outdoors dangerous.
A gale swept through the coastal town overnight.

words.english_meaning: A thin layer of ice crystals that forms on surfaces when temperature drops below freezing.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઠંડીમાં સપાટી પર જામેલા બરફના ઝીણા સ્ફટિક — જ્યારે તાપમાન શૂન્ય ડિગ્રી નીચે જાય.
words.usage_note: Frost appears overnight and melts after sunrise; affects crops badly.
words.memory_tip: 'Frost' → 'ફ્રોઝ' (freeze) → freeze = જામી ગયેલ → frost = જામેલ બરફ.
examples: A heavy frost damaged the crops overnight.
The grass was covered with frost in the morning.
Frost warnings were issued for the region.
The frost made the roads slippery.

words.english_meaning: A mixture of rain and snow, or partly melted snow falling as icy pellets.
words.gujarati_meaning: વરસાદ અને બરફ ભેગા પડે — અડધા ઓગળેલા બરફના ઝીણા ટુકડા જ્યારે પડે.
words.usage_note: Common in cold temperate climates; different from hail which is larger.
examples: The forecast predicted sleet for the weekend.
Sleet made driving conditions very hazardous.
Children were disappointed when snow turned to sleet.
The sleet stung our faces as we walked.

words.english_meaning: A prolonged period of abnormally hot weather.
words.gujarati_meaning: લાંબા સમય સુધી ચાલુ રહેતી અસામાન્ય ગરમ હવામાનની સ્થિતિ.
words.usage_note: A heatwave lasts several days and poses serious health risks.
examples: A severe heatwave struck northern India last June.
Hospitals were overwhelmed during the heatwave.
The heatwave caused widespread power outages.
Farmers suffered huge losses due to the heatwave.

words.english_meaning: A severe snowstorm with strong winds and low visibility.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભારે બરફ અને જોરદાર પવન સાથે આવતું ભીષણ હિમ-તોફાન — જ્યાં કાંઈ દેખાય નહીં.
words.usage_note: A blizzard requires winds of at least 56 km/h with snow reducing visibility.
examples: A blizzard paralyzed the city for three days.
Rescue teams struggled through blizzard conditions.
The blizzard left over a metre of snow.
Schools were closed during the blizzard.

words.english_meaning: A thick cloud of tiny water droplets near the ground reducing visibility.
words.gujarati_meaning: જમીન પાસે ઝીણા પાણીના ટીપાંનો ઘટ્ટ ગુચ્છ — જેથી આગળ ઓછું દેખાય.
words.usage_note: Fog differs from mist by having visibility below 1 km.
words.memory_tip: 'Fog' → 'ફ' = ફસાઈ ગયા (got stuck) → ફૉગમાં ફસાઈ જવાય.
examples: Dense fog caused several accidents on the highway.
The fog lifted by mid-morning.
Flights were delayed due to heavy fog.
The old lighthouse guided ships through the fog.

words.english_meaning: Unpleasantly warm and damp; oppressively humid.
words.gujarati_meaning: અગવડ ભરી ગરમ અને ભેજવાળી હવા — જ્યારે શ્વાસ લેવો પણ ભારે લાગે.
words.usage_note: Informal word often used to describe tropical monsoon weather.
examples: The muggy afternoon made everyone feel lethargic.
It was too muggy to enjoy the outdoor festival.
A muggy breeze offered no real relief.
The muggy climate of Kerala takes getting used to.

words.english_meaning: Having a light, refreshing wind blowing.
words.gujarati_meaning: હળવો, તાજો પવન ફૂંકાતો હોય — ઠંડક આપનારો.
words.usage_note: Breezy implies a pleasant, light wind — unlike windy which can be unpleasant.
words.memory_tip: 'Breeze' = ઠંડો પવન → 'breezy' = ઠંડો પવન વાળો દિવસ.
examples: A breezy afternoon made the beach perfect.
The breezy weather was ideal for flying kites.
She wore a light scarf on the breezy morning.
The breezy hilltop offered a stunning view.

words.english_meaning: Any form of water — rain, snow, sleet — that falls from clouds to the ground.
words.gujarati_meaning: વાદળોમાંથી જમીન પર પડતું કોઈ પણ સ્વરૂપનું પાણી — વરસાદ, બરફ, કે ઝીણા બરફ.
words.usage_note: Scientific/meteorological term used in weather reports and geography.
words.memory_tip: 'Precipi-' = ઝડપથી પડવું → precipitation = આકાશમાંથી ઝડપથી પડતું પાણી.
examples: The region receives over 2000 mm of precipitation annually.
Low precipitation has led to drought conditions.
Meteorologists measure precipitation using rain gauges.
The precipitation this winter was mostly in the form of snow.

words.english_meaning: The loud rumbling or crashing sound heard during a thunderstorm, caused by lightning.
words.gujarati_meaning: વીજળી ચમકે ત્યારે સંભળાતો ભારે ગડગડાટ — ગૂઢ મોટો અવાજ.
words.usage_note: Thunder is the sound; lightning is the light. They occur together in storms.
examples: The children hid under the blanket at the thunder.
A loud clap of thunder woke everyone up.
Thunder rolled across the mountains.
We heard distant thunder as the storm approached.

words.english_meaning: A violently rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm to the ground.
words.gujarati_meaning: ગર્જનાતોફાનમાંથી જમીન સુધી ફૂંકાતો ઝડપભેર ફરતો હવાનો સ્તંભ — અત્યંત વિનાશકારી.
words.usage_note: Tornadoes are measured on the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale from EF0 to EF5.
examples: A tornado destroyed dozens of homes in the town.
Residents took shelter as a tornado warning was issued.
The tornado left a path of destruction 2 km wide.
Scientists study tornadoes to improve early warning systems.

words.english_meaning: The distance one can see clearly, especially in relation to weather conditions.
words.gujarati_meaning: હવામાનમાં કેટલે દૂર સ્પષ્ટ દેખી શકાય — ખાસ કરીને ધુમ્મસ, ધૂળ કે વરસાદ વખતે.
words.usage_note: Used heavily in aviation, marine, and road safety contexts.
examples: Fog reduced visibility to less than 50 metres.
Pilots reported poor visibility at the airport.
Visibility improved once the rain stopped.
Low visibility caused a multi-car accident on the highway.

words.english_meaning: A seasonal wind bringing heavy rainfall, especially in South and Southeast Asia.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઋતુ-પ્રમાણે ફૂંકાતો પવન — ખાસ કરીને ભારત-એશિયામાં ભારે વરસાদ લઈ આવે.
words.usage_note: In India, the southwest monsoon arrives around June and retreats by October.
examples: The monsoon arrived two weeks early this year.
Farmers eagerly await the monsoon season.
Heavy monsoon rains flooded low-lying areas.
The monsoon is essential for India's agriculture.

words.english_meaning: The time when the sun crosses the equator, making day and night equal in length.
words.gujarati_meaning: જ્યારે સૂર્ય વિષુવવૃત્ત પર હોય — દિવસ અને રાત સરખી લંબાઈ ધરાવે.
words.usage_note: Occurs twice a year: around March 20 and September 23.
examples: The spring equinox marks the start of astronomical spring.
On the equinox, day and night are each 12 hours long.
Many cultures celebrate the autumn equinox.
The equinox occurs around March 20 each year.

words.english_meaning: Either of the two times of year when the sun reaches its furthest point north or south, giving the longest or shortest day.
words.gujarati_meaning: વર્ષમાં બે વખત — જ્યારે સૂર્ય સૌથી ઉત્તર અથવા દક્ષિણ બિંદુ પર હોય — સૌથી લાંબો કે ટૂંકો દિવસ.
words.usage_note: Summer solstice (~June 21) is the longest day; winter solstice (~Dec 21) the shortest.
words.memory_tip: 'Sol' = સૂર્ય (sun) + 'stice' = ઊભા રહેવું → સૂર્ય જ્યાં ઊભો રહે.
examples: The summer solstice is celebrated with bonfires in many cultures.
June 21 is the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere.
The solstice marks an important point in the astronomical calendar.
Stonehenge was built to align with the summer solstice sunrise.

words.english_meaning: Having a mild climate without extremes of heat or cold.
words.gujarati_meaning: સૌમ્ય આબોહવા — ન ખૂબ ગરમ, ન ખૂબ ઠંડી — સામાન્ય, અનુકૂળ હવામાન.
words.usage_note: The temperate zones lie between the tropics and the polar regions.
examples: Britain has a temperate maritime climate.
Temperate forests support a wide variety of wildlife.
The temperate zone experiences four distinct seasons.
Grapes grow well in temperate climates.

words.english_meaning: Relating to regions adjacent to the tropics, with hot summers and mild winters.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉષ્ણકટિબંધ નજીકના પ્રદેશ — ગરમ ઉનાળો અને સૌમ્ય શિયાળો ધરાવે.
words.usage_note: Gujarat and parts of western India have a subtropical climate.
examples: Gujarat has a subtropical climate with hot summers.
Subtropical regions experience heavy monsoon rainfall.
Many citrus fruits thrive in subtropical climates.
The subtropical zone lies between the tropics and temperate regions.

words.english_meaning: In a state of rest or inactivity; temporarily inactive (used of plants, animals, or volcanoes).
words.gujarati_meaning: આરામ કે નિષ્ક્રિયતાની અવસ્થામાં — ઋતુ પ્રમાણે ઘણા છોડ, પ્રાણી કે જ્વાળામુખી નિષ્ક્રિય રહે.
words.usage_note: Used in biology for plants in winter and animals in hibernation.
examples: Many plants remain dormant during the cold winter months.
The volcano had been dormant for over a century.
Seeds lie dormant in the soil until spring arrives.
Bears become dormant during hibernation.

words.english_meaning: Lasting or existing for a long or apparently infinite time; (of plants) living for several years.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઘણા વર્ષો સુધી જીવતો/ચાલુ રહેતો — (છોડ માટે) દર વર્ષે ફૂલ આપે.
words.usage_note: In gardening, perennials return every year; annuals last only one season.
examples: Roses are popular perennial garden plants.
Flooding is a perennial problem in low-lying areas.
Perennial rivers flow throughout the year.
This perennial grass survives drought and frost.

words.english_meaning: To melt or cause to melt from ice or snow; to become warmer after winter.
words.gujarati_meaning: બરફ ઓગળવો — ઠંડી ઘટ્યા પછી બરફ ઓગળે અથવા ઠંડા ખોરાક/વ્યક્તિ ગરમ થઈ જાય.
words.usage_note: Also used figuratively: 'relations between countries began to thaw.'
examples: The ice on the lake began to thaw in March.
Frozen pipes thawed after the temperature rose.
The spring thaw flooded the meadows.
She left the meat out to thaw before cooking.

words.english_meaning: A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall leading to water shortage.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઘણા સમય સુધી ઓછો વરસાદ — જળ-સંકટ ઊભો થાય.
words.usage_note: Drought affects agriculture, water supply, and ecosystems.
examples: The region suffered its worst drought in 50 years.
Drought forced many farmers to abandon their crops.
The government declared a drought emergency.
Drought-resistant crops are vital in arid regions.

words.english_meaning: A violent, windy storm.
words.gujarati_meaning: ભારે પવન અને વરસાদ સાથેનું ભીષણ તોફાન.
words.usage_note: Mostly literary/poetic; 'A tempest in a teapot' means a big fuss over something small.
examples: The sailors feared the tempest would sink their ship.
Shakespeare's play 'The Tempest' features a magical storm.
The tempest lasted three days and caused widespread damage.
A tempest of emotions swept through the crowd.

words.english_meaning: The typical weather conditions of a region over a long period.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ પ્રદેશની લાંબા સમય સુધીની સામાન્ય હવામાન-પ્રકૃતિ — આબોહવા.
words.usage_note: Climate is long-term patterns; weather is day-to-day conditions.
words.memory_tip: 'Climate' → ક = કાયમ (permanent) → કાયમ ની હવા = આબોહવા.
examples: India has a tropical climate in most regions.
Climate change is one of the biggest global challenges.
The Mediterranean climate is ideal for olive growing.
Scientists study climate patterns to predict future weather.

words.english_meaning: Relating to spring; fresh and young.
words.gujarati_meaning: વસંત ઋતુ સાથે સંબંધિત — તાજો, નવો, ઉત્સાહભર્યો.
words.usage_note: Mostly used in formal or poetic contexts to refer to spring.
examples: The vernal equinox occurs around March 20.
Vernal flowers bloomed across the meadow.
The air had a vernal freshness after the long winter.
Vernal pools are temporary ponds that form in spring.

words.english_meaning: Relating to autumn; characteristic of autumn.
words.gujarati_meaning: પાનખર ઋતુ સંબંધી — જ્યારે પાંદડાં ખરે અને ઠંડી શરૂ થાય.
words.usage_note: Used in poetic or formal contexts for autumn.
examples: The park was bathed in autumnal colours of red and gold.
An autumnal chill filled the evening air.
The autumnal equinox marks the start of fall.
Autumnal festivals celebrate the harvest season.

words.english_meaning: Ground that remains permanently frozen, found in polar and subarctic regions.
words.gujarati_meaning: ધ્રુવ પ્રદેશોમાં સ્થાયી રૂપે જામેલ ભૂમિ — ક્યારેય ઓગળતી નથી.
words.usage_note: Thawing permafrost due to climate change releases greenhouse gases.
examples: Permafrost covers about 25% of the Earth's land surface.
Melting permafrost is accelerating climate change.
Buildings in Siberia are constructed on permafrost.
Ancient organisms have been found preserved in permafrost.

words.english_meaning: The recurring process of water evaporating, forming clouds, and falling as precipitation.
words.gujarati_meaning: પાણી બાષ્પ બને, વાદળ બને, અને ફરી વરસાદ/બરફ રૂપે પડે — આ ફરી ફરી ચાલતી પ્રક્રિયા.
words.usage_note: Also called the hydrological cycle; fundamental to Earth's climate system.
words.memory_tip: 'Cycle' = ચક્ર → precipitation cycle = વરસાદ-ચક્ર = water cycle.
examples: The precipitation cycle is essential for life on Earth.
Deforestation disrupts the natural precipitation cycle.
Students learn about the precipitation cycle in geography.
The precipitation cycle distributes fresh water across the planet.

words.english_meaning: (Of trees) shedding leaves seasonally, especially in autumn.
words.gujarati_meaning: (વૃક્ષ) જે ઋતુ-ક્રમ અનુસાર — ખાસ પાનખરમાં — પાંદડાં ખેરવે.
words.usage_note: Contrasted with evergreen trees that keep their leaves year-round.
words.memory_tip: 'Decide' + '-uous' → deciduous = (ઋતુ) નક્કી કરે ત્યારે પાન ખરે.
examples: Oak and maple are common deciduous trees.
Deciduous forests are stunning in autumn colours.
Deciduous trees lose their leaves to conserve water in winter.
The park is dominated by deciduous woodland.

words.english_meaning: The pressure exerted by the atmosphere at any point, used in weather forecasting.
words.gujarati_meaning: વાયુ-મંડળ જે દબાણ ઊભું કરે — હવામાનની આગાહી માટે ઉપયોગી.
words.usage_note: Low pressure usually brings rain; high pressure brings clear skies.
examples: Falling barometric pressure signals an approaching storm.
Weather forecasters monitor barometric pressure closely.
A sudden drop in barometric pressure preceded the typhoon.
Barometric pressure is measured in millibars or hectopascals.

words.english_meaning: A piece of land almost surrounded by water, connected to mainland on one side.
words.gujarati_meaning: ત્રણ બાજુ પાણીથી ઘેરાયેલ અને એક બાજુ ભૂ-ભાગ સાથે જોડાયેલ જમીન-ટૂકડો.
words.usage_note: India is a peninsula; Gujarat has the Kathiawar (Saurashtra) peninsula.
examples: The Arabian Peninsula is the world's largest peninsula.
Kerala lies on the southern tip of the Indian Peninsula.
The Saurashtra peninsula juts into the Arabian Sea.
The peninsula was connected to the mainland by a narrow strip of land.

words.english_meaning: A flat area of high ground; an elevated tableland.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઊંચાઈ પર આવેલ સપાટ ભૂ-પ્રદેશ — ઉચ્ચ-ભૂમિ.
words.usage_note: The Deccan Plateau covers much of peninsular India.
words.memory_tip: 'Plateau' = 'plate' (flat plate) + 'au' → flat like a plate on high ground.
examples: The Deccan Plateau covers most of southern India.
The Tibetan Plateau is the highest in the world.
The plateau offered a panoramic view of the surrounding plains.
Plateau regions often have cooler temperatures than surrounding areas.

words.english_meaning: A narrow valley between hills or mountains, usually with a river flowing through it.
words.gujarati_meaning: ડુંગરો વચ્ચે ઊંડી અને સાંકડી ખીણ — નીચે નદી વહે.
words.usage_note: Formed by river erosion over millions of years; different from a canyon in scale.
examples: The river carved a spectacular gorge through the mountains.
We hiked through the narrow gorge for three hours.
The gorge was home to rare ferns and mosses.
Rafting in the gorge was an unforgettable experience.

words.english_meaning: The wide part of a river's mouth where it meets the sea, affected by tides.
words.gujarati_meaning: નદીનું મોં — જ્યાં નદી સમુદ્ર સાથે ભળે — ભરતી-ઓટ અહીં અનુભવાય.
words.usage_note: Estuaries are highly productive ecosystems supporting diverse species.
words.memory_tip: 'Estuary' → 'east' → 'river goes east to sea' → estuary = river meets sea.
examples: The Thames Estuary is one of Europe's busiest waterways.
Mangroves often grow in tropical estuaries.
The estuary provides habitat for migratory birds.
Many cities are built near estuaries for trade and transport.

words.english_meaning: A vast, flat, treeless Arctic region with permanently frozen subsoil.
words.gujarati_meaning: ધ્રુવ પ્રદેશ નજીક — ઝાડ-ઝાંખરા વિહોણો વિશાળ, સપાટ, સ્થાયી-બરફ ભૂ-ભાગ.
words.usage_note: The tundra has permafrost below, a short growing season, and low biodiversity.
words.memory_tip: 'Tundra' → ઠ-ઠ-ઠ = ઠંડા ઠેકાણા (freezing place) → ઠંડો વિસ્તાર.
examples: Reindeer and polar bears live in the tundra.
The Arctic tundra is warming faster than any other biome.
Low shrubs and mosses are typical tundra vegetation.
The tundra seems barren but supports a unique ecosystem.

words.english_meaning: A slowly moving mass of ice formed by accumulated snow over many years.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઘણા વર્ષો સુધી જામેલ હિમ — ધીમે ધીમે ખસતો વિશાળ બરફ-ભૂ.
words.usage_note: Glaciers are retreating worldwide due to climate change.
words.memory_tip: 'Glaci-' = glassy ice → glacier = કાચ જેવો વિશાળ બરફ-ભૂ.
examples: The Gangotri glacier is the source of the Ganges river.
Glaciers around the world are melting at alarming rates.
A glacial valley has a distinctive U-shaped profile.
Scientists drill ice cores from glaciers to study past climates.

words.english_meaning: A stretch of shallow seawater separated from the sea by a reef, sandbar, or similar feature.
words.gujarati_meaning: ખારા/મીઠા છીછરા પાણીનો ઘેરો — ખડક કે રેતી-ટીંબા દ્વારા સમુદ્રથી અલગ.
words.usage_note: Coral lagoons form inside atolls; coastal lagoons form along shorelines.
words.memory_tip: 'Lagoon' → 'L' = lake-like → shallow like a lake near the sea.
examples: The turquoise lagoon was perfect for snorkelling.
Chilika Lagoon in Odisha is Asia's largest coastal lagoon.
The coral reef protected the lagoon from ocean waves.
Flamingos flocked to the shallow salt lagoon.

words.english_meaning: A grassy plain in tropical or subtropical regions, with few trees.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉષ્ણ-ઉષ્ણકટિબંધ પ્રદેશોમાં ઘાસ-ઢંકાયેલ વિશાળ મેદાન — ઝાડ ઓછાં.
words.usage_note: The African savanna is home to elephants, lions, and wildebeest.
examples: Lions hunt on the African savanna.
The savanna has distinct wet and dry seasons.
Giraffes roam the East African savanna.
Fire is a natural part of the savanna ecosystem.

words.english_meaning: Land that is saturated with water, either permanently or seasonally, such as marshes and swamps.
words.gujarati_meaning: કાયમ અથવા ઋતુ-ક્રમ પ્રમાણે પાણી-ભૂ —늪, ભેખડ, ખારો ઝૂ.
words.usage_note: Wetlands filter water, store carbon, and support rich biodiversity.
examples: Wetlands serve as natural water filters.
The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove wetland.
Millions of migratory birds depend on wetlands.
Wetland destruction has led to declining amphibian populations.

words.english_meaning: A deep open crack in a glacier or snowfield.
words.gujarati_meaning: ગ્લૅશિયર અથવા બરફ-ભૂ પર ઊઘડેલ ઊંડી ફાટ — ખૂબ જોખમકારક.
words.usage_note: Crevasses are extremely dangerous for mountaineers and glaciologists.
examples: The mountaineer narrowly avoided falling into a crevasse.
Crevasses form where a glacier moves over uneven terrain.
They used ropes to cross the dangerous crevasse.
Snow bridges over crevasses can collapse without warning.

words.english_meaning: The flat area beside a river that is covered with water when the river floods.
words.gujarati_meaning: નદી કિનારે આવેલ સપાટ ભૂ — પૂર વખતે ડૂબી જાય.
words.usage_note: Floodplains are very fertile due to sediment deposition but are flood-prone.
examples: The Nile floodplain is one of the most fertile in the world.
Building on floodplains increases the risk of flood damage.
The floodplain was covered with rich alluvial soil.
Communities on floodplains must have effective early warning systems.

words.english_meaning: A group or chain of islands scattered in a large body of water.
words.gujarati_meaning: મોટા જળ-ક્ષેત્રમાં ફેલાયેલ ટાપુઓ-સમૂહ.
words.usage_note: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago with over 17,000 islands.
words.memory_tip: 'Archi' = chief + 'pelago' = sea → chief sea = sea full of islands.
examples: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago.
The Lakshadweep archipelago lies in the Arabian Sea.
The archipelago offered stunning diving spots.
Sea level rise threatens many low-lying archipelagos.

words.english_meaning: A deep gorge, typically with a river flowing through it, often in an arid region.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઊંડી, ઢોળાવ-ભરી ખીણ — ખૂ-ભ (dry) પ્રદેશમાં — નીચે નદી.
words.usage_note: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is the most famous canyon in the world.
words.memory_tip: 'Canyon' → 'can' = ઠ-ઠ → 'can you see the bottom?' → ઊંડી ખીણ.
examples: The Grand Canyon was carved by the Colorado River.
The canyon walls displayed millions of years of geological history.
Hiking into the canyon takes several hours.
Eagles nest on the sheer walls of the canyon.

words.english_meaning: A long, narrow, deep inlet of the sea between steep cliffs, formed by glacial erosion.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઊભા-ઢોળ ખડકો વચ્ચે ઊંડી, સાંકડી, લાંબી ખાડી — ગ્લૅશિયર ઘસારાથી બની.
words.usage_note: Norway is famous for its spectacular fjords; they are UNESCO-listed.
words.memory_tip: 'Fjord' → 'F' = ફ = ફાટ (split) → ખડક ફાટ = ઊંડી ખાડી.
examples: Norway's fjords attract millions of tourists every year.
The Sognefjord is the longest fjord in the world.
Cruise ships navigate slowly through the deep fjords.
The fjord was surrounded by snow-capped mountains.

words.english_meaning: A ridge of rock in the sea formed by the growth of coral, supporting diverse marine life.
words.gujarati_meaning: સમુદ્રમાં પ્રવાળ (coral) ઉગ્યો અને ખડક-ટ્ટ જેવી રચના — ઘણા દરિયાઈ જીવ-જંતુઓ ત્યાં રહે.
words.usage_note: Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support 25% of marine species.
examples: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system.
Coral reefs are dying due to ocean warming and acidification.
Divers explore the coral reef for its brilliant colours.
Coral reefs protect coastlines from storm waves.

words.english_meaning: A landform created by sediment deposited where a river meets a body of water, often fan-shaped.
words.gujarati_meaning: નદી જ્યાં સમુદ્ર/સરોવરને મળે ત્યાં જામેલ કાંપ-માટી — ત્રિકોણ આકારની ભૂ-રચના.
words.usage_note: The Sundarbans delta (Ganges-Brahmaputra) is the world's largest river delta.
words.memory_tip: Delta = ∆ (ત્રિકોણ) → triangle shape where river meets sea.
examples: The Nile Delta is one of the most fertile farming regions.
The Sundarbans mangrove forest grows in the Ganges Delta.
The city of New Orleans is built on the Mississippi Delta.
River deltas are rich in biodiversity and agriculture.

words.english_meaning: A mound or ridge of sand formed by wind, especially in deserts or near coasts.
words.gujarati_meaning: પવન વડે ઢેરો થઈ ગયેલ રેતીનો ઢૂવો — રણ કે દરિયા-કિનારે.
words.usage_note: Dunes constantly shift shape due to wind; some reach 100+ metres high.
words.memory_tip: 'Dune' → 'D' = desert → desert + mound = sand dune = રેતીનો ઢૂવો.
examples: The Thar Desert is famous for its vast sand dunes.
Tourists ride camels across the golden dunes.
Coastal dunes protect shorelines from erosion.
The dunes shifted overnight due to strong winds.

words.english_meaning: A tree or shrub that grows in coastal saline or brackish water in tropical regions.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉષ્ણ-દરિયા-કિનારા પર ખારા અથવા ઓછા ખારા પાણીમાં ઉગ્યો — ઊભા મૂળ ધરાવ — ચેર-ઝાડ.
words.usage_note: Mangroves protect coastlines from erosion and storms, and support rich biodiversity.
words.memory_tip: 'Man' + 'grove' → a grove for the sea-man → દરિયા-કિનારા પર ઝૂ.
examples: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest.
Mangroves act as natural barriers against cyclones.
Many fish species breed in mangrove swamps.
Gujarat's coastal mangroves are being restored by NGOs.

words.english_meaning: A forest dominated by trees that shed their leaves annually during autumn or dry season.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઋતુ-ક્રમ અનુસાર — ઉનાળે અથવા પાનખરે — બધા ઝાડ પાન ખેરવે — તેવો જંગલ.
words.usage_note: Tropical deciduous forests cover large parts of central India.
words.memory_tip: 'Deciduous' = ઝાડ (trees) decided to drop leaves = ઋતુ-ક્રમ અનુસાર પાન ખેરવ.
examples: India's deciduous forests burst into colour after the monsoon.
Teak and sal trees dominate deciduous forests in India.
Wildlife sanctuaries are often set in deciduous forests.
The deciduous forest floor is rich in leaf litter.

words.english_meaning: The transfer of pollen from one flower to another, enabling plant fertilization.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક ફૂલથી બીજા ફૂલ પર પરાગ-ટ્રાન્સફર — ફળ-ઉત્પત્તિ શક્ય બને.
words.usage_note: Bees are the most important pollinators; without them food production collapses.
examples: Bees play a crucial role in the pollination of crops.
Without pollination, many plants cannot produce fruit.
Pollination can occur via wind, insects, or birds.
Declining bee populations threaten pollination worldwide.

words.english_meaning: The process by which green plants use sunlight to synthesize food from carbon dioxide and water.
words.gujarati_meaning: લીલા છોડ સૂર્ય-પ્રકાશ, CO₂ અને પાણી વડે ખોરાક ઉત્પન્ન કરે — ઓક્સિજન ઉત્સર્જ.
words.usage_note: Produces oxygen as a by-product — essential for all aerobic life.
examples: Photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy.
Without photosynthesis, there would be no oxygen on Earth.
The rate of photosynthesis increases with more light.
Scientists are studying artificial photosynthesis for clean energy.

words.english_meaning: To spend the winter in a dormant state, with greatly reduced metabolic activity.
words.gujarati_meaning: શિયાળો ઊંઘ-અવસ્થામાં — ઘણા ઓછા ચયાપચય સાથે — વિતાવવો.
words.usage_note: Bears, hedgehogs, and some bats hibernate; they live off stored fat.
examples: Bears hibernate from November through March.
Some snakes hibernate in rocky dens during winter.
Hibernating animals reduce their heart rate dramatically.
Scientists study hibernation for insights into human medicine.

words.english_meaning: The use of colours or patterns to blend into the natural environment and avoid detection.
words.gujarati_meaning: આ-પ-પ-ઉ (surroundings) સ-ઉ (with) ભ-ળ-ઉ (blend) — દ-ઉ (enemy) ન-ઉ (cannot see) — camouflage = છૂ-પ-ઉ (hide).
words.usage_note: Many animals use camouflage to hunt or avoid predators.
examples: The chameleon is famous for its natural camouflage.
Arctic foxes turn white in winter as camouflage against snow.
Leaf insects have evolved perfect camouflage.
Camouflage patterns are used in military uniforms.

words.english_meaning: The seasonal movement of animals from one region to another, typically for feeding or breeding.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઋતુ-ક્રમ અનુસાર પ્રાણી/પક્ષી ખોરાક અથવા પ્રજ-ઉ-ઉ (breeding) માટે દૂ-ર (far) પ્રવ-ઉ-ઉ (journey).
words.usage_note: The wildebeest migration in Africa and bird migration to India are iconic examples.
words.memory_tip: 'Migrate' = move across → migration = ઋ-ઉ-ઉ (seasonal) moving = પ-ઉ-ઉ (journey).
examples: Flamingos migrate to Gujarat's Rann of Kutch in winter.
The wildebeest migration is called the Great Migration.
Climate change is altering bird migration patterns.
Millions of butterflies migrate to Mexico every autumn.

words.english_meaning: An animal that hunts, kills, and eats other animals.
words.gujarati_meaning: બ-ઉ-ઉ (other) પ-ઉ-ઉ (animals) ખ-ઉ (eat) — ઉ (hunt and kill for food) — predator = ઉ-ઉ (hunter).
words.usage_note: Apex predators like tigers and lions are at the top of the food chain.
examples: The tiger is an apex predator in Indian forests.
Predators control the population of prey animals.
The loss of predators disrupts the ecological balance.
Wolves are being reintroduced to control deer populations.

words.english_meaning: A complex network of living organisms and their physical environment interacting together.
words.gujarati_meaning: સ-ઉ-ઉ (all organisms) + ઉ-ઉ-ઉ (environment) = એ-ઉ (a network of life) — ecosystem = જ-ઉ-ઉ-ઉ (life-network).
words.usage_note: Disrupting one part of an ecosystem affects all other parts.
examples: The Amazon rainforest is the world's most biodiverse ecosystem.
Coral reefs are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth.
Human activity is destroying natural ecosystems rapidly.
Restoring ecosystems can help combat climate change.

words.english_meaning: The leaves of a plant or tree collectively.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઝ-ઉ (tree)/છ-ઉ (plant) ન-ઉ (of) ઉ (all) પ-ઉ (leaves) — collectively — foliage = ઉ-ઉ (leafage).
words.usage_note: 'Foliage' is used in a formal or botanical context; 'leaves' is more everyday.
words.memory_tip: 'Folio' = leaf/page → foliage = many leaves = ઝ-ઉ ન-ઉ (tree's) leaves.
examples: The autumn foliage of New England attracts many tourists.
Dense foliage kept the forest floor cool.
The foliage of the tropical tree provides habitat for birds.
Heavy rain knocked the foliage from the trees.

words.english_meaning: A group of living organisms able to interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (organisms) ન-ઉ (of) ઉ-ઉ (same kind) — that can breed together — species = ઉ-ઉ (type/kind).
words.usage_note: There are an estimated 8.7 million species on Earth, most still undiscovered.
words.memory_tip: 'Species' → 'spec' = special kind → species = special type of life.
examples: The Bengal tiger is an endangered species.
Scientists discovered a new species of frog in the Amazon.
Protecting species diversity is vital for ecosystem health.
India hosts over 500 species of migratory birds.

words.english_meaning: The uppermost layer of a forest formed by the crowns of the tallest trees.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (forest) ન-ઉ (of) ઉ-ઉ (tallest trees) ઉ-ઉ (crowns) — roof-like top layer — canopy = ઉ-ઉ (tree-roof).
words.usage_note: The canopy intercepts most sunlight; organisms below are adapted to shade.
examples: The rainforest canopy is home to monkeys and toucans.
Little sunlight penetrates the dense canopy to the forest floor.
Scientists study canopy life using elevated walkways.
The canopy acts as a shield against heavy rain.

words.english_meaning: The variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat or on Earth.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (all) પ-ઉ/ઉ-ઉ (plants/animals) ઉ-ઉ (variety) — bio-diversity = ઉ-ઉ (life variety).
words.usage_note: India is one of the 17 megadiverse countries in the world.
examples: The Amazon rainforest has unparalleled biodiversity.
India is a megadiverse country with rich biodiversity.
Biodiversity loss threatens food security and medicine.
Protected areas are essential for preserving biodiversity.

words.english_meaning: Active at night rather than during the day.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (night) ઉ-ઉ (active) — that which is active at night — nocturnal = ઉ-ઉ (night-active).
words.usage_note: Owls, bats, and leopards are examples of nocturnal animals.
examples: Owls are nocturnal hunters with excellent night vision.
The leopard is a nocturnal predator.
Many desert animals are nocturnal to avoid daytime heat.
Scientists use infrared cameras to study nocturnal wildlife.

words.english_meaning: A close, long-term interaction between two different species, often mutually beneficial.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (two) ઉ-ઉ (different) ઉ-ઉ (species) ઉ-ઉ (close) ઉ-ઉ (relationship) — often both benefit — symbiosis.
words.usage_note: Bees and flowers, clownfish and sea anemones are classic examples.
examples: The relationship between bees and flowers is a form of symbiosis.
Clownfish and sea anemones have a symbiotic relationship.
Fungi and tree roots form symbiosis called mycorrhizae.
Symbiosis allows both organisms to thrive in harsh environments.

words.english_meaning: A plant with thick, fleshy leaves or stems that store water, adapted to arid conditions.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (water) ઉ-ઉ (store) — ઉ-ઉ (thick leaves/stems) — dry climate adaptable plant — succulent.
words.usage_note: Cacti are the most well-known succulents; aloe vera is a widely used succulent.
words.memory_tip: 'Succulent' = juicy (succulent food) → plant that's 'juicy' inside = stores water.
examples: Aloe vera is a widely used succulent with medicinal properties.
Succulents are popular houseplants because they need little water.
Desert succulents survive months without rainfall.
The cactus is the most iconic succulent of the Sonoran Desert.

words.english_meaning: The ecological interaction where one organism (predator) hunts and feeds on another (prey).
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (predator) ઉ-ઉ (hunts) ઉ-ઉ (prey) — ઉ-ઉ (ecological) ઉ-ઉ (balance) — predator-prey relationship.
words.usage_note: Loss of predators leads to prey overpopulation and ecosystem imbalance.
words.memory_tip: Predator = hunter; prey = hunted → predator-prey = hunter-hunted relationship.
examples: The wolf-deer predator-prey relationship keeps forest ecosystems balanced.
Studying predator-prey relationships helps in wildlife conservation.
A disrupted predator-prey dynamic can collapse entire ecosystems.
The cheetah-gazelle predator-prey relationship is studied globally.

words.english_meaning: The large-scale clearing of forests, permanently destroying them for other land use.
words.gujarati_meaning: જંગલો કાપી-નાખ — મોટા પ્રમાણ પર — ખેતી, ઉ-ઉ (industry) અ-ઉ (or) ઉ-ઉ (construction) ઉ-ઉ (for).
words.usage_note: Deforestation releases carbon dioxide and destroys habitat; major driver of climate change.
examples: Deforestation in the Amazon threatens thousands of species.
India loses millions of hectares to deforestation each year.
Deforestation contributes to soil erosion and flooding.
NGOs are working to reverse deforestation in tribal areas.

words.english_meaning: The total amount of greenhouse gases, especially carbon dioxide, produced by a person or activity.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (person/activity) ઉ-ઉ (total) CO₂ ઉ-ઉ (release) — carbon footprint.
words.usage_note: Reducing your carbon footprint involves eating less meat, flying less, using renewable energy.
words.memory_tip: 'Footprint' = ઉ-ઉ (mark you leave) → carbon footprint = ઉ-ઉ (CO₂) mark you leave.
examples: Flying has a very high carbon footprint.
Companies are measuring and reducing their carbon footprint.
Switching to electric vehicles lowers your carbon footprint.
Schools teach students how to calculate their carbon footprint.

words.english_meaning: The warming of the Earth caused by gases in the atmosphere trapping heat from the sun.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (atmosphere) ઉ-ઉ (gases) ઉ-ઉ (trap heat) — ઉ-ઉ (Earth) ઉ-ઉ (warms up).
words.usage_note: The greenhouse effect is natural and necessary; the enhanced version due to human activities causes global warming.
words.memory_tip: ઉ-ઉ (glass greenhouse traps warmth) → Earth's atmosphere does the same = greenhouse effect.
examples: The greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life.
Human activities are enhancing the greenhouse effect.
CO₂, methane, and water vapour are key greenhouse gases.
Understanding the greenhouse effect is essential for climate science.

words.english_meaning: The thinning of the ozone layer in the atmosphere, increasing UV radiation reaching Earth.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (ozone layer) ઉ-ઉ (thin) ઉ-ઉ (UV rays) ઉ-ઉ (Earth reach) = ozone depletion.
words.usage_note: CFCs from aerosols were the main cause; the Montreal Protocol helped recovery.
examples: Ozone depletion over Antarctica led to the 'ozone hole'.
CFC gases were banned to slow ozone depletion.
Ozone depletion increases the risk of skin cancer.
The ozone layer is slowly recovering thanks to global action.

words.english_meaning: The introduction of harmful substances into the environment, damaging it.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (environment) ઉ-ઉ (harmful substances) ઉ-ઉ (intro) — ઉ-ઉ (damage).
words.usage_note: There are many types: air, water, soil, noise, and light pollution.
examples: Air pollution in Delhi reaches dangerous levels in winter.
Industrial pollution has contaminated the river.
Noise pollution affects mental health in cities.
Strict laws are needed to curb plastic pollution.

words.english_meaning: Rain made acidic by atmospheric pollution, harming vegetation and water bodies.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (pollutants) ઉ-ઉ (rain + mix) → ઉ-ઉ (acidic rain) ઉ-ઉ (harms plants/water).
words.usage_note: Caused by SO₂ and NOₓ from burning fossil fuels; damages forests, lakes, and buildings.
examples: Acid rain killed vast areas of forest in Europe in the 1980s.
Marble monuments are dissolving due to acid rain.
Power plants burning coal release gases that cause acid rain.
International agreements have reduced acid rain significantly.

words.english_meaning: Capable of being broken down naturally by bacteria or other living organisms.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (bacteria/organisms) ઉ-ઉ (naturally break down) — biodegradable.
words.usage_note: Biodegradable materials return to nature; non-biodegradable ones persist for centuries.
words.memory_tip: 'Bio' = life + 'degrade' = break down → breaks down by life = biodegradable.
examples: Paper and cotton are biodegradable materials.
Switching to biodegradable packaging reduces plastic waste.
Food waste is biodegradable and can be composted.
Not all 'eco-friendly' plastics are truly biodegradable.

words.english_meaning: The gradual wearing away of soil, rock, or land by wind, water, or other forces.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (wind/water) ઉ-ઉ (soil/rock) ઉ-ઉ (gradually wear away) — erosion.
words.usage_note: Deforestation accelerates erosion; roots hold soil in place.
words.memory_tip: 'Erode' = ઉ-ઉ (eat away) → erosion = ઉ-ઉ (eating away) of land.
examples: Coastal erosion is threatening cliffs and beaches.
Soil erosion reduces agricultural productivity.
Planting trees is an effective way to prevent erosion.
Erosion carved the spectacular landforms of Badlands National Park.

words.english_meaning: The ability to meet present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (present needs) ઉ-ઉ (meet) ઉ-ઉ (future) ઉ-ઉ (compromise no) — sustainability.
words.usage_note: The UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) address global sustainability challenges.
words.memory_tip: 'Sustain' = ટ-ઉ-ઉ (keep going) + '-ability' = ability → ability to keep going = sustainability.
examples: Sustainability is central to modern urban planning.
Solar energy is key to environmental sustainability.
Companies are adopting sustainability reporting practices.
The UN SDGs promote global sustainability by 2030.

words.english_meaning: Energy from sources that are naturally replenished, such as solar, wind, or hydro power.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (solar/wind/water) ઉ-ઉ (naturally refill) — renewable energy.
words.usage_note: India aims to achieve 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030.
examples: Solar panels are the fastest-growing source of renewable energy.
India is a world leader in renewable energy expansion.
Renewable energy reduces dependence on imported oil.
Wind farms generate renewable energy without emissions.

words.english_meaning: Long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns, largely driven by human activities.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (global) ઉ-ઉ (temperature/weather) ઉ-ઉ (long-term change) — mostly human-caused.
words.usage_note: The IPCC reports that limiting warming to 1.5°C requires urgent global action.
examples: Climate change is causing more frequent extreme weather events.
The Paris Agreement aims to limit climate change to 1.5°C.
Small island nations face existential threats from climate change.
Young activists are demanding action on climate change.

words.english_meaning: The destruction or degradation of a natural environment that plants and animals depend on.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (animals/plants) ઉ-ઉ (home/environment) ઉ-ઉ (destroy/degrade) — habitat loss.
words.usage_note: Habitat loss is the primary driver of species extinction worldwide.
words.memory_tip: 'Habitat' = ઉ-ઉ (home) + 'loss' = ઉ-ઉ (destroy) → losing home = habitat loss.
examples: Habitat loss is the biggest threat to tigers in India.
Urban expansion causes widespread habitat loss.
Conservation corridors help mitigate habitat loss effects.
Habitat loss and poaching have pushed rhinos to near extinction.

words.english_meaning: A condition where the number of people or animals in an area exceeds what resources can sustainably support.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (people/animals) ઉ-ઉ (too many) — ઉ-ઉ (resources) ઉ-ઉ (not enough) — overpopulation.
words.usage_note: Overpopulation strains resources, increases pollution, and drives habitat loss.
words.memory_tip: 'Over' = ઉ-ઉ (too much) + 'population' = ઉ-ઉ (people) → too many people.
examples: Overpopulation in cities leads to housing and water shortages.
Wildlife overpopulation can strip an area of vegetation.
Deer overpopulation in suburbs causes crop and garden damage.
Sustainable development addresses challenges posed by overpopulation.

words.english_meaning: The process by which fertile land becomes desert, often due to drought and overuse.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (fertile land) ઉ-ઉ (desert) ઉ-ઉ (become) — usually drought + overuse caused.
words.usage_note: The Sahel region of Africa faces severe desertification; the Great Green Wall project combats it.
examples: Overgrazing is accelerating desertification in arid regions.
Desertification threatens food security for millions.
The Great Green Wall aims to stop desertification across Africa.
Planting drought-resistant trees can reverse desertification.

words.english_meaning: The long-term storage of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to reduce greenhouse gases.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (CO₂) ઉ-ઉ (long-term store) — forests/soil/ocean ઉ-ઉ (trap) CO₂.
words.usage_note: Forests are the most effective natural carbon sinks; oceans absorb about 30% of CO₂.
words.memory_tip: 'Sequester' = ઉ-ઉ (hold apart/store) → carbon sequestration = store carbon away.
examples: Forests are vital for carbon sequestration.
Peatlands store more carbon than all the world's forests combined.
Carbon sequestration technology is being developed for power plants.
Protecting wetlands enhances natural carbon sequestration.

words.english_meaning: The deterioration of the natural environment through depletion of resources and destruction of ecosystems.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (natural environment) ઉ-ઉ (resources deplete) ઉ-ઉ (ecosystems destroy) — deterioration.
words.usage_note: Addressing environmental degradation requires both policy and individual action.
words.memory_tip: 'Degrade' = ઉ-ઉ (reduce quality) → environmental degradation = reducing environment's quality.
examples: Rapid industrialisation has caused severe environmental degradation.
Environmental degradation reduces the quality of life in rural areas.
The UN calls environmental degradation a global emergency.
Community-based conservation can reverse environmental degradation.

words.english_meaning: A sudden violent shaking of the ground caused by movements of the Earth's tectonic plates.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (tectonic plates) ઉ-ઉ (move) → ઉ-ઉ (ground) ઉ-ઉ (shake violently) — earthquake.
words.usage_note: Measured on the Richter scale or moment magnitude scale; above 7.0 is very strong.
examples: The 2001 Bhuj earthquake devastated Gujarat.
Earthquake-resistant buildings are essential in seismic zones.
A 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck Turkey in 2023.
Early warning systems can save lives during earthquakes.

words.english_meaning: A series of giant ocean waves caused by an underwater earthquake, landslide, or volcanic eruption.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (underwater earthquake/eruption) ઉ-ઉ (giant waves) ઉ-ઉ (coast) ઉ-ઉ (hit) — tsunami.
words.usage_note: The 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami killed over 200,000 people across 14 countries.
words.memory_tip: Japanese word: 'tsu' = harbour + 'nami' = wave → harbour wave = tsunami.
examples: The 2004 tsunami devastated coastal areas across Southeast Asia.
A tsunami warning system was established after 2004.
Tsunamis can travel at 800 km/h across open ocean.
Coastal communities practise tsunami evacuation drills.

words.english_meaning: A large, destructive system of winds rotating around a centre of low pressure over the ocean.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (ocean) ઉ-ઉ (low pressure centre) ઉ-ઉ (rotating winds) — ઉ-ઉ (destructive).
words.usage_note: Called hurricane in Atlantic, typhoon in Pacific, cyclone in Indian Ocean.
examples: Cyclone Biparjoy hit Gujarat's coast in June 2023.
A severe cyclone warning was issued for Odisha's coast.
Cyclones draw energy from warm ocean water.
Thousands were evacuated before the cyclone made landfall.

words.english_meaning: The sudden release of magma, gases, and ash from a volcano onto the Earth's surface.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (volcano) ઉ-ઉ (lava/ash/gases) ઉ-ઉ (suddenly release) — volcanic eruption.
words.usage_note: Can affect global climate by releasing ash and sulphur dioxide into the atmosphere.
words.memory_tip: 'Erupt' = ઉ-ઉ (burst out) → volcanic eruption = ઉ-ઉ (lava burst).
examples: The 1980 Mount St Helens eruption caused massive destruction.
Volcanic eruptions can disrupt air travel with ash clouds.
Indonesia sits on the Ring of Fire and has frequent eruptions.
Lava from the eruption reached the sea within hours.

words.english_meaning: The rapid movement of a mass of earth, rock, or debris down a hillside.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (hill) ઉ-ઉ (soil/rock/debris) ઉ-ઉ (rapidly slide down) — landslide.
words.usage_note: Common during monsoons in hilly regions; deforestation increases landslide risk.
examples: A landslide buried the mountain village during heavy rain.
Deforestation increases the risk of landslides.
The Wayanad landslide of 2024 was one of India's deadliest.
Early warning systems can reduce landslide casualties.

words.english_meaning: A sudden, violent flood caused by extremely heavy rainfall in a short time.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (sudden heavy rain) → ઉ-ઉ (rapid flooding) — flash flood.
words.usage_note: Flash floods can occur with little warning; particularly dangerous in valleys and urban areas.
words.memory_tip: 'Flash' = ઉ-ઉ (sudden, like flash of light) + 'flood' = ઉ-ઉ (flood) → sudden flood.
examples: A flash flood swept through the desert canyon without warning.
Flash floods in Himachal Pradesh killed dozens in 2023.
Urban areas are increasingly prone to flash floods.
People should never try to drive through a flash flood.

words.english_meaning: An uncontrolled fire that spreads rapidly through vegetation in rural or wilderness areas.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (uncontrolled fire) ઉ-ઉ (forest/rural) ઉ-ઉ (rapid spread) — wildfire.
words.usage_note: Climate change is making wildfires more frequent and severe.
words.memory_tip: 'Wild' = ઉ-ઉ (uncontrolled, in the wild) + 'fire' = ઉ-ઉ (fire) → wildfire.
examples: Wildfires burned millions of hectares in Australia in 2019-2020.
Climate change is making wildfire seasons longer and more intense.
Firefighters battled the wildfire for weeks before containing it.
Wildfires release huge amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

words.english_meaning: An abnormal rise of water level along a coast due to storm winds pushing sea water ashore.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (storm) ઉ-ઉ (winds) ઉ-ઉ (push seawater) ઉ-ઉ (coast) — storm surge.
words.usage_note: Storm surges are the deadliest aspect of hurricanes and cyclones for coastal communities.
words.memory_tip: 'Surge' = ઉ-ઉ (sudden rise) + storm → storm surge = sudden sea rise during storm.
examples: The storm surge during Cyclone Amphan flooded Kolkata's streets.
Storm surges are more dangerous than the wind itself.
Coastal embankments protect against storm surges.
Low-lying island nations are most vulnerable to storm surges.

words.english_meaning: A large mass of snow and ice that suddenly falls down a mountain.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (mountain) ઉ-ઉ (snow/ice mass) ઉ-ઉ (suddenly fall) — avalanche.
words.usage_note: Avalanches can be triggered by heavy snowfall, vibrations, or warming temperatures.
examples: An avalanche buried the ski resort in metres of snow.
Mountaineers carry avalanche beacons for safety.
Loud sounds can trigger an avalanche on unstable slopes.
Avalanche warnings were issued across the Himalayan region.

words.english_meaning: A critical state of water shortage declared when drought causes severe humanitarian or economic crisis.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (water shortage) ઉ-ઉ (severe crisis) ઉ-ઉ (declared emergency) — drought emergency.
words.usage_note: Governments declare drought emergencies to mobilize resources for affected regions.
examples: The state declared a drought emergency after three failed monsoons.
Drought emergencies trigger food and water relief programmes.
Climate change is increasing the frequency of drought emergencies.
Farmers demand compensation during declared drought emergencies.

words.english_meaning: The frequency, type, and size of earthquakes and ground movement in a region over a period of time.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (earthquakes/ground movement) ઉ-ઉ (frequency/type/size) — seismic activity.
words.usage_note: Seismographs record seismic activity; seismologists study earthquake patterns.
examples: Seismic activity in the Himalayan region is closely monitored.
Increased seismic activity preceded the volcanic eruption.
Scientists use GPS to track seismic activity and plate movement.
Gujarat lies in a high seismic activity zone.

words.english_meaning: A smaller earthquake that follows the main earthquake in the same area.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (main earthquake) ઉ-ઉ (after) ઉ-ઉ (same area) ઉ-ઉ (smaller quake) — aftershock.
words.usage_note: Aftershocks can be nearly as strong as the main quake and cause additional damage.
words.memory_tip: 'After' + 'shock' = ઉ-ઉ (after) + ઉ-ઉ (shock) → shock that comes after.
examples: Dozens of aftershocks followed the main earthquake.
Rescue workers are always alert to aftershocks during operations.
A powerful aftershock collapsed already weakened buildings.
Aftershocks can continue for weeks after a major earthquake.

words.english_meaning: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (earthquake origin) ઉ-ઉ (directly above surface point) — epicentre.
words.usage_note: The epicentre experiences the strongest shaking; damage decreases with distance.
words.memory_tip: 'Epi-' = above + 'centre' = ઉ-ઉ (centre) → the centre point above the quake origin.
examples: The epicentre of the earthquake was 20 km north of the city.
Buildings near the epicentre were completely flattened.
Scientists located the epicentre using seismograph data.
The epicentre of the 2001 Bhuj quake was in Kutch district.

words.english_meaning: An official alert issued by meteorological authorities warning of an approaching dangerous storm.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (meteorological) ઉ-ઉ (official alert) ઉ-ઉ (dangerous storm approaching) — storm warning.
words.usage_note: Storm warnings are issued in colour codes (yellow, orange, red) based on severity.
examples: A storm warning was issued for the entire coastal district.
Residents were advised to stay indoors during the red storm warning.
The storm warning allowed thousands to evacuate in time.
Weather agencies improve storm warnings using satellite data.

words.english_meaning: The flooding and submersion of a flat area beside a river during high water levels.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (river) ઉ-ઉ (high water) → ઉ-ઉ (floodplain) ઉ-ઉ (submerge) — inundation.
words.usage_note: Regular inundation deposits fertile silt; but excessive flooding devastates communities.
words.memory_tip: 'Inundate' = ઉ-ઉ (flood over) → inundation = submersion in water.
examples: The annual inundation of the Nile enriched Egypt's farmlands.
Flood plain inundation in Bihar affects millions of farmers.
Inundation maps help identify areas at risk of flooding.
The floodplain was inundated for weeks after the dam overflow.

words.english_meaning: A storm in which hail (balls of ice) falls, sometimes causing severe damage to crops and property.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (ice balls) ઉ-ઉ (fall in storm) — ઉ-ઉ (crops/property damage) — hailstorm.
words.usage_note: Hailstones can be as large as golf balls or bigger; cause millions in crop damage annually.
examples: A hailstorm destroyed most of the wheat crop in minutes.
Large hailstones shattered car windscreens across the city.
Farmers lost their entire harvest to a sudden hailstorm.
Hailstorm warnings are issued by meteorological departments in spring.
